intro: {@vocation_director} has an office in the chancery with a window onto the parking lot and a filing cabinet that is, this month, mostly you. On the desk are the application, the psychologist’s report, the letters from your pastor and from two people you did not know had been asked, and a legal pad. He says this is not an examination, which is what men say before examinations, and that the bishop and the rector will read what he writes. He does not say you will not.
close: He caps the pen. He says the notes go to the bishop and to the rector and that you will not see them, which is true, and that most of what he wrote he could have guessed from the application, which is not. He walks you to the parking lot and shakes your hand. {seminary} begins on Monday.

questions.prompt: He uncaps the pen. “Start where everyone starts. Why a priest, and why now? Not the version from the application.”

answers.label: “Because I have known since I was a boy, and I ran out of reasons not to.”
answers.outcome: He writes one line and does not look up. “The boys who knew are the ones who leave in second year or stay for fifty. I have not worked out how to tell which.”

effects.value: Has wanted this since boyhood and says so plainly. Either the real thing or a habit.

answers.label: “Because of a priest I knew. I would like to be that for someone.”
answers.outcome: “What was his name?” You tell him. He writes it down, which you did not expect. “The best reason there is, and the one that breaks first when the priests you meet turn out to be men.”

effects.value: Came because of a good priest. The best reason and the most fragile; he will need to meet another.

answers.label: “I lost an argument with God. I had been losing it for some years.”
answers.outcome: The pen stops. “That is a convert’s answer,” he says, “and you were baptised at three weeks. Keep it. Say it in the propaedeutic year when the silence gets long.”

effects.value: Speaks of a struggle he lost to God. A convert’s language in a cradle Catholic; the propaedeutic year will tell whether it is a story or a wound.

answers.label: “I am not sure. That is part of why I am here.”
answers.outcome: He looks up for the first time. “Good. The men who are sure arrive with the answer and leave when the question changes. You will be less comfortable than they are and you will last longer. Probably.”

effects.value: Honest and uncertain in the first five minutes. I would rather that than certainty; the rector may not.

questions.prompt: “Sunday. The ten-thirty at an ordinary parish of this diocese: a cantor with a microphone, a deacon who preaches too long, Communion in the hand, a child crying through the consecration. You are in the pew. What do you make of it?”

answers.label: “I would rather the older Mass, and I am not going to pretend otherwise in your office.”
answers.outcome: “No,” he agrees, “don’t. Pretend in the rector’s.” He writes two lines. “There are four parishes in this diocese where that answer makes you a pastor by forty and sixty where it makes you a problem. I will remember which you want.”

effects.value: Prefers the older form and said so in the first hour, unasked. Place him with care.

answers.label: “It is the Mass. I would say it reverently and let the rest sort itself out.”
answers.outcome: “That is the answer the bishop gives,” he says, “and I have never been sure whether he means it.” He writes one line. “It is the right answer. The parishes will want to know which rest you mean.”

effects.value: Sound on the liturgy and without an agenda he will own to. Will be easy to place.

answers.label: “It is where the people are. I would meet them there and not make them feel they were doing it wrong.”
answers.outcome: “The child crying,” he says. “Do you stop and wait, or go on?” You answer. He nods as if he had heard both answers before and liked them about equally.

effects.value: At home in the ordinary parish Mass and warm about the people in it. The traditional parishes will not want him; the rest will.

answers.label: “I would want to know why the deacon preaches too long before I judged anything.”
answers.outcome: “Because no one has told him,” he says, “for eleven years. You will be the one who tells him. Write that down somewhere; you will want to remember you said it.”

effects.value: Would not be drawn on the liturgy and asked about the deacon instead. Slow to judge, or careful of me.

questions.prompt: “Fifteen years from now. Not what you think I want to hear and not what you think the bishop wants. Where are you?”

answers.label: “A pastor. A parish with a school and a debt, and people who know my name at the grocery store.”
answers.outcome: “You will have the debt,” he says. “Most men who say that mean it, and the diocese runs on the ones who do.” He underlines something.

effects.value: Wants a parish and nothing else he will admit to. The diocese needs forty of him.

answers.label: “Rome. The College for theology, a degree after. I know how that sounds.”
answers.outcome: “It sounds like a man who has read the biographies,” he says, “and some of them were written about men who said it in this chair.” He writes it down without comment, and puts a mark beside it you cannot read upside down. “The rector will hear you want it. That is not the same as going.”

effects.value: Wants Rome, the College and a degree, and said so at the first interview. Either the real article or a boy who has read too much; the rector should hear it either way.

answers.label: “Wherever the bishop needs a man who can read a budget and keep his mouth shut.”
answers.outcome: “We have those,” he says. “We are always short of them.” He writes a longer line than the others. “You understand the second half of that is the hard half.”

effects.value: Has the temperament for the chancery and asked for it, which is unusual and useful. Discreet, I think.

answers.label: “Teaching. A classroom at the seminary, a library, men being formed well.”
answers.outcome: “By men who were formed badly,” he says, “which is the joke the faculty tell about themselves.” He writes it down. “You will need the degree first, and the degree needs the grades. I will tell the rector you are a man to watch in the philosophy years.”

effects.value: Wants the seminary faculty. Watch the philosophy marks.

answers.label: “I try not to think fifteen years ahead. I would like to be a good priest and to still be one.”
answers.outcome: He does not write anything for a moment. “That is either the best answer anyone has given me this year or the most careful. I will know by Christmas.”

effects.value: No ambitions he will admit to. Rare, or careful; either is fine.

questions.prompt: “Your first summer. I place the men, and I place them before they have earned anything, so this is the only time your asking counts for much. The hospital. A city parish with more funerals than baptisms. The Spanish course in Guatemala. Or a desk in this building. Where would you want to be?”

answers.label: “The hospital.”
answers.outcome: “The supervisor there is a Lutheran woman who has made more priests than this seminary,” he says. “She will not like you for the first month.” He writes your name on a second pad.

effects.value: Asked for the hospital for his first summer, unprompted.

answers.label: “The parish with the funerals.”
answers.outcome: “The pastor is seventy-one and has buried the parish twice,” he says. “He will give you the eleven o’clock and the Thursday funeral and not much else, and you will learn more from him than from anyone here.”

effects.value: Asked for the hard parish. Good instinct or bravado; the summer will say.

answers.label: “Guatemala. I want the Spanish before I need it.”
answers.outcome: “You will need it,” he says. “Everyone in this diocese needs it by their second parish and most of them learn it there, badly.” He writes a line and adds a word to it.

effects.value: Wants the Spanish early. Sensible; the diocese is short of it.

answers.label: “Here. I would like to see how the diocese actually runs.”
answers.outcome: He looks at you over the pad. “It runs on four women in the next office and a man in Finance who has not taken a holiday since the Clinton administration. You can see it. The priests will notice that you asked.”

effects.value: Asked for the chancery in his first summer. Ambitious, or curious about the machinery; I could not tell.

questions.prompt: “A case. You are a deacon in your last summer. The pastor tells you to do something you think is wrong. Not sinful; wrong. A bad decision about the school, say, that will hurt people in a year. What do you do?”

answers.label: “I do it. He is the pastor and I am not.”
answers.outcome: “Yes,” he says, and writes. “And in a year, when it hurts people?” You answer. He writes that too.

effects.value: Obedient, and said so without hesitating. Possibly too obedient; the parish will find the limit before the chancery does.

answers.label: “I tell him once, in private, what I think and why. Then I do it.”
answers.outcome: He nods slowly. “That is the answer,” he says, “and you got to it faster than most. The hard part is the once.”

effects.value: Found the right answer on the pastor case quickly: speak once, in private, then obey. Will be a good vicar.

answers.label: “I tell him, and I keep telling him until he hears it.”
answers.outcome: “He will hear it,” he says. “He will hear it at the deanery meeting and from the bishop’s secretary and from his own housekeeper, and in his report on you he will use the word ‘collaborative’ in a way the board knows how to read.”

effects.value: Would keep pressing a pastor who had decided. Will be a difficult vicar and perhaps a good pastor.

answers.label: “If it will hurt people, I go to the bishop.”
answers.outcome: The pen stops again. “Over a school decision.” He lets it sit. “The bishop would see you. He would also remember that you came.”

effects.value: Went over the pastor’s head in a hypothetical and would do it in life. The presbyterate will know him for it within a year.

questions.prompt: “Money. You will have less of it than your friends and more of other people’s than you have ever seen, in a safe in a rectory with a lock from 1962. Tell me about you and money.”

answers.label: “I have never had much and I do not miss it.”
answers.outcome: “You will have a car,” he says, “and a parish will give you a better one, and that is where it starts. I say that to everyone.”

effects.value: Indifferent to money, he says. Most are, until the car.

answers.label: “I had a salary. I know what I am giving up and I have done the arithmetic.”
answers.outcome: “Good. Do it again in year four, when the men you started with are buying houses.” He writes something and underlines it. “A parish will want that arithmetic. They are not good at it.”

effects.value: Left a salary and knows the sum. Will keep a parish’s books; may be hard on a parish that cannot.

answers.label: “Other people’s money frightens me a little. I think it should.”
answers.outcome: “It should,” he says, “and it stops frightening everyone, and the ones it stops frightening first are the ones I read about.” He writes two words.

effects.value: The right fear about money. Keep it in him.

answers.label: “I am good with it. A parish is a small business and most of them are badly run.”
answers.outcome: “Most of them are,” he agrees, “by men who were told in this chair that a parish is not a business. Both of you are right and only one of you will be popular.”

effects.value: Talks about a parish like a manager. Useful in a parish with a debt; a problem in one with a soul.

questions.prompt: “Who do you call at eleven at night when something has gone wrong? Not who should you call. Who do you call.”

answers.label: “My family.”
answers.outcome: “Keep calling them,” he says. “The house will try to be your family and it is not; it is a house.”

effects.value: Calls his family when things go wrong. Good.

answers.label: “Friends from before. Some of them think I am making a mistake.”
answers.outcome: “The ones who think so are the ones to keep,” he says. “They will still be there if they are right.”

effects.value: Has friends outside the Church who doubt this. Keep them; the house should not be his only room.

answers.label: “A priest. The one I mentioned.”
answers.outcome: He writes the name again, or looks at where he wrote it. “He will not be able to hear your confession once you are in the house, you understand. Someone else will have to be eleven o’clock.”

effects.value: Leans on a priest he knows. Fine, so long as it is not the only leaning.

answers.label: “Nobody. I handle things.”
answers.outcome: He puts the pen down. “Then the house will be that for you, or a bar will. I have watched both. I am writing this down so that someone asks you the question again in two years.”

effects.value: Has no one he calls when things go wrong. The house must become that, or something worse will. Ask again in two years.

questions.prompt: “There is a page in your file that you wrote yourself, about before. I have read it. I would rather hear it from you than carry only the page.”

answers.label: “Ask me anything you want. I would rather you heard it all now.”
answers.outcome: He asks three questions, none of them the ones you expected, and writes less than you feared. “Thank you. Most men make me work for it.”

effects.value: Spoke about the past without being pushed, and answered what I asked. I believe him.

answers.label: “It is in the file. I would rather not go over it again.”
answers.outcome: “All right.” He does not press. “You will go over it again, though. With the director, and with the board, and with yourself at three in the morning in a rectory. I would get used to it.”

effects.value: Would not discuss the past. Not hiding it, I think; tired of it. The board will want more.

answers.label: “I have dealt with it. It is part of why I am here, not something that happened before I was.”
answers.outcome: “That is the answer the psychologist likes,” he says, and writes, “and I like it too, when it is true. We will see whether it holds in the quiet.”

effects.value: Speaks of the past as a part of the vocation. Well integrated, or well rehearsed; the propaedeutic year will tell.

questions.prompt: “You left a career. Men who leave careers for this either never look back or look back every day, and I cannot tell which from the application. Which will you be?”

answers.label: “Never. It was a job. This is not.”
answers.outcome: “You will look back once,” he says, “when a classmate from the firm is made partner. Once is allowed.”

effects.value: Left a career and does not look back. Says.

answers.label: “I will miss it, and I will use it. There is nothing I learned there that a parish does not need.”
answers.outcome: “There is one thing,” he says, “but you will find out which. The rest, yes.” He writes a longer line.

effects.value: Brings a career with him and knows what in it is useful. The chancery will find him before the parishes do.

answers.label: “Every day, probably. I am doing it anyway.”
answers.outcome: “That is the honest answer,” he says. “The men who give it mostly stay. I do not know why.”

effects.value: Honest about the cost of leaving a career. Will carry it; most who admit it do.

questions.prompt: “Last thing. The bishop asks me every August which of the new men he should know by name. He does not mean it kindly or unkindly; he means he has sixty priests to place and likes to know who is coming. Should I give him yours?”

answers.label: “Yes.”
answers.outcome: He writes it. “He will know your name by the Chrism Mass, and he will watch how you serve it. Do not drop anything.”

effects.value: Wanted the bishop to know his name from the first week. Confident or ambitious; I could not tell which, and told the bishop so.

answers.label: “Not yet. Ask me again in a year, when there is something to tell him.”
answers.outcome: He looks at you for a moment longer than he has all hour. “I will.” He writes something short. “That is the first time anyone has said that in this chair.”

effects.value: Asked me to wait a year before the bishop heard his name. I liked that more than I should say.

answers.label: “Give him the names of the men who need him to know them. I will be all right.”
answers.outcome: “You may not be,” he says, “but I take the point.” He writes it. “The men who need him will not thank you. That is the deal.”

effects.value: Asked me to put the bishop onto the men who needed him rather than himself. A brother already, or a good imitation.
